People deserve more from their money. More visibility, more control, and more freedom. Since 2015, Revolut has been on a mission to deliver just that. Our powerhouse of products — including spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more — help our 80+ million customers get more from their money every day.

# Senior Software Engineer (Frontend) - Design System & Mobile (x/f/m) - Paris or Nantes

Unlimited Contract

Paris

Engineering

## About Doctolib

At Doctolib, we’re reinventing the daily lives of health professionals and empowering people to live healthier across Europe.

More than 3,000 Doctolibers across France, Germany, Italy, the UK and the Netherlands are building a new generation of AI-powered technologies and services, trusted by 520 000 health professionals and over 90 million patients every day.

AI is at the heart of how we build and how we work. At Doctolib, AI fluency is a core skill for every team member: we foster a culture leveraging AI to drive efficiency, quality, and impact at scale.

## Job description

## What we do

Join a team of passionate and hardworking entrepreneurs to transform healthcare! Working in the tech team at Doctolib involves building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients. We work in feature teams in an agile environment, while collaborating with engineering, design, and business teams.

## What you'll do

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Design System & Accessibility Team and help us become the #1 digital and secure medical companion for patients.

We are part of the Platform domain, whose mission is to build and maintain the common building blocks of our system with a "Platform as a Product" mindset. We abstract and simplify the use of these complex, critical components, enabling product teams to focus on their core mission: building products faster for healthcare professionals and patients.

Why this role matters: With 80% of Doctolib's traffic coming from mobile, we're on a mission to bridge the gap between our Web and Mobile Design Systems. You'll be a key player in unifying the user experience across platforms.

As a Frontend Platform team, we support and empower all other Doctolib Tech and Product teams to create Accessible and best-in-class user experience frontend applications. We achieve our mission by providing a web and mobile design system, by writing supporting tooling around it and the Accessibility topic, and guidance as Accessibility experts.

As a Senior Software Engineer, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

* Design, build, and maintain a scalable Web and mobile Design System built with React and React Native, ensuring a consistent, accessible, and high-performance user experience across Doctolib's web and mobile applications.
* Drive the convergence of Web and Mobile Design Systems, ensuring visual and functional consistency across React and React Native components.
* Develop and maintain React Native components, enabling seamless cross-platform experiences.
* Upskill and mentor team members on React Native best practices, fostering a culture of mobile-first thinking within the Design System team.
* Work hand-in-hand with Product Designers to translate Figma designs into robust, reusable UI

# Senior Frontend Engineer (m/f/d)

Remote, Leer

Full-time

Permanent employee

## Role

Everything our users see runs on Next.js and React, and we'd like to hand it to you: the design system it's built from, how fast it loads, and whether everyone can actually use it.

You'll work closely with our software architects, product owners, and fellow developers: code reviews, pair programming, and the technical decisions that stick around.

## Your mission

* You build and maintain our design system in React and Tailwind, so features stay consistent instead of being rebuilt from scratch each time.
* You own frontend performance in Next.js 16 — rendering strategy, bundle size, and what people actually experience on a mediocre connection.
* You treat accessibility as a default, not as cleanup at the end of the sprint.
* You develop the Node.js layer (Express.js, Nest.js) between the UI and our backend services, with Redis where caching helps.
* You push for clean code and automated testing, and you share what you know instead of sitting on it.
* You use coding agents as part of your daily workflow — directing their work, reviewing their output, and fixing what doesn't hold up. Writing code matters; knowing what good code looks like matters more.

## Your profile

* You've spent several years building production frontends with React, Next.js, and TypeScript.
* You know Tailwind CSS well and you've managed client-side state with Zustand.
* You test what you build — unit and component tests with Vitest, end-to-end tests with Playwright.
* You're comfortable in Node.js with Express.js or Nest.js, and working against APIs from a microservices backend.
* You work well in agile teams (Scrum/Kanban), you write clearly, and you're comfortable in English.
* You have a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field — or the experience that makes one unnecessary.

## Nice to have

* You've worked with AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform. We're not in the cloud yet, so this is a plus, not a requirement.

## How you think

We care as much about how you approach a problem as about which frameworks you know. You look past the edges of your own ticket: you notice when a fix really belongs in a different service, you question a process once it has stopped making sense, and you judge your work by whether the whole system got better — not by whether your part shipped. "Not my code" isn't a sentence we use much around here.

## Why us?

You're joining at a point where the engineering foundations themselves are being rebuilt around AI-native workflows — not retrofitted onto legacy decisions, but designed now, while the architecture is still being shaped. That means you don't inherit someone else's five-year-old choices: you help make the calls on how services are split, where AI agents fit into the workflow, and what "good" looks like technically around here.
